question_en: Does the startup navigator determine which rules apply?
question_sv: Avgör startup-navigatorn vilka regler som gäller?
target_construct: potential regulatory relevance of a scenario
proxy_measure: editorial scenario rules linking answers to articles and obligations
conclusion_en: Traceable pointers to possibly relevant rules, not a legal classification.
conclusion_sv: Spårbara hänvisningar till möjligen relevanta regler, inte en juridisk klassificering.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Legal applicability
diagnostics.interpretation: The navigator identifies potentially relevant rules; it does not determine legal applicability, which depends on facts, annexes, delegated acts, standards and national law.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Navigator references that point at an existing article or obligation
diagnostics.interpretation: The rules only point at provisions that exist in the current text. That makes them traceable; it does not make them a legal classification.

question_en: Are obligations assigned to the right topic (for example transparency)?
question_sv: Är skyldigheterna tilldelade rätt ämne (till exempel transparens)?
proxy_measure: a curated assignment in seeds/eu_ai_act/ai_act_obligations.csv, each with a verbatim quote
conclusion_en: Quotes are verified; topics are an unreviewed editorial reading.
conclusion_sv: Citaten är verifierade; ämnena är en ogranskad redaktionell läsning.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Independent review of the topic assignments
diagnostics.interpretation: The quotes are checked against the official text; the topic each obligation is filed under is one editor's reading and has not been reviewed by a second person.

question_en: Did the AI Act change how often AI is discussed in the Riksdag and in job ads?
question_sv: Ändrade AI-förordningen hur ofta AI diskuteras i riksdagen och i jobbannonser?
target_construct: effect of the Act on political and labour-market language
proxy_measure: monthly shares on one time axis with the Act's milestones

diagnostics.diagnostic: Ratio of the AI share in job ads, 2025 to 2022
diagnostics.interpretation: The rise starts after the public launch of generative AI (November 2022), which overlaps with the Act's negotiation; the data cannot separate the two. Temporal overlap does not prove causation.

confounders.remaining_risk: cannot be separated with this data

question_en: Is corpus identity driving the shared space?
question_sv: Är det korpusen som styr det gemensamma rummet?
proxy_measure: similarity of chunks to curated anchor sentences in one multilingual model
conclusion_en: Language is handled; corpus identity dominates, which is why the layer compares corpora only through ranks.
conclusion_sv: Språket är hanterat; korpusen dominerar, därför jämförs korpusarna bara genom rangordning.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Swedish anchors whose nearest English anchor is the same concept
diagnostics.interpretation: The Swedish and English anchor sentences say the same thing to the model, so language alone does not move a concept.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Nearest neighbours from the same corpus, over chance
diagnostics.interpretation: The corpora differ far more than their subjects do, so chunks are compared only through the concepts (rank within a chunk), never on one map.

confounders.mitigation: compare only through concept ranks within a chunk and z-scores within a corpus

question_en: Do job ads measure labour-market demand?
conclusion_en: Job ads are a proxy for demand on one platform, not the labour market.
conclusion_sv: Jobbannonser är en indikator på efterfrågan på en plattform, inte arbetsmarknaden.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Size of the change in Data/IT's share of all ads, first to latest full year (percentage points)
diagnostics.interpretation: A term's share can move because the mix of occupations moved. Data/IT's share of ads has barely changed, so the rise of AI terms is not explained by more IT ads; mix shifts within fields are not measured.

diagnostics.diagnostic: What the ads cover
diagnostics.interpretation: Many jobs are filled without an ad on this platform (recruiters, networks, internal moves); job ads are a proxy for demand, not the labour market itself.

question_en: Does a term's frequency in ads measure employers' demand for the skill?
question_sv: Mäter en terms frekvens i annonser arbetsgivares efterfrågan på kompetensen?
proxy_measure: share of ads whose headline or description matches the term's pattern
conclusion_en: Term shares describe the words in ads. Without a reviewed sample they are a weak proxy for skill demand.
conclusion_sv: Termandelar beskriver orden i annonserna. Utan ett granskat urval är de en svag indikator på kompetensefterfrågan.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Repeated ad ids within an archive (removed before counting)
diagnostics.interpretation: Republished ads with the same id are counted once; near-identical ads with new ids (templates, chains) are not detected.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Boilerplate and template text
diagnostics.interpretation: Privacy and GDPR terms often come from a standard notice about how applications are handled, not from the job; no sample of matches has been reviewed.

confounders.diagnostic: Data/IT share of ads over time
confounders.effect: a term's share moves with the mix
new words for the same skill are missed
confounders.mitigation: patterns in both languages with variants

question_en: Do the groups follow ideas, or works and translators?
question_sv: Följer grupperna idéer, eller verk och översättare?
proxy_measure: multilingual sentence embeddings of passages, UMAP and HDBSCAN, raw and centred per work
conclusion_en: Centring reduces work and translator dominance; neither is removed, and no group is named without review.
conclusion_sv: Centrering minskar verkens och översättarnas dominans; ingen av dem försvinner, och ingen grupp namnges utan granskning.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Nearest neighbours from the same work, over chance (raw map)
diagnostics.interpretation: Passages sit next to passages of their own work far more often than chance.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Nearest neighbours from the same work, over chance (centred per work)
diagnostics.interpretation: Centring lowers the effect but the work still shapes the space.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Nearest neighbours with the same translator, over chance (centred per work)
diagnostics.interpretation: The translator's English remains a confounder alongside the work.

question_en: Does the roll-call division index measure political polarisation?
question_sv: Mäter delningsindexet för voteringar politisk polarisering?
proxy_measure: per roll call, 1 − the largest same-position bloc's share of members voting, averaged per policy area
conclusion_en: A descriptive measure of division in recorded votes, not of polarisation.
conclusion_sv: Ett beskrivande mått på delning i voteringar, inte på polarisering.

diagnostics.diagnostic: What the index counts
diagnostics.interpretation: It measures how the parties divided on the items that reached a recorded vote. That is division in voting, not polarisation of opinion or ideology, and which items reach a roll call is itself a political choice.

confounders.effect: only items that reach a roll call are measured

question_en: Do Riksdag speeches represent political opinion?
target_construct: what parties and politicians think about an issue
proxy_measure: what is said in the chamber
conclusion_en: Speeches show the chamber's language, not opinion in general.
conclusion_sv: Anförandena visar språket i kammaren, inte åsikter i allmänhet.

diagnostics.diagnostic: What the corpus covers
diagnostics.interpretation: Chamber speeches are a formal, agenda-driven genre; they leave out committee work, media and everything not said in the chamber.

question_en: Can a party's vote be predicted from the other parties' positions, and does the evaluation hold up?
question_sv: Kan ett partis röst förutsägas från de andra partiernas ståndpunkter, och håller utvärderingen?
target_construct: how predictable a party's vote is from the rest of the chamber
proxy_measure: gradient boosting trained on one riksmöte and tested on the next, against always guessing the majority
conclusion_en: The evaluation is sound, but accuracy above the majority baseline is the measure, and it holds for only some parties.
conclusion_sv: Utvärderingen är sund, men träffsäkerhet över majoritetsgissningen är måttet, och den gäller bara för vissa partier.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Train and test sessions are different
diagnostics.interpretation: Training and testing on different sessions keeps the same roll call from appearing on both sides.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Share of parties where the model beats always guessing the majority
diagnostics.interpretation: For parties that nearly always vote yes, the majority guess is already right and the model adds nothing; for some it does worse. Predictability is not agreement, coalition or polarisation.

confounders.diagnostic: accuracy against the majority baseline per party
confounders.mitigation: report the baseline beside every accuracy

question_en: Does semantic similarity between speeches and the AI Act show that the debate responded to the Act?
question_sv: Visar semantisk likhet mellan anföranden och AI-förordningen att debatten svarade på förordningen?
target_construct: influence of the Act on the debate
proxy_measure: cosine similarity of multilingual sentence embeddings, above a random-pair baseline
conclusion_en: Semantic similarity, nothing more; influence is not measured.
conclusion_sv: Semantisk likhet, inget mer; påverkan mäts inte.

diagnostics.diagnostic: 95th percentile of similarity for random speech–article pairs
diagnostics.interpretation: Pairs above chance use related language. Related language is not influence, and the measure cannot tell the two apart.

question_en: Do the clusters reflect symbolic meaning, or which book a passage comes from?
question_sv: Speglar klustren symbolisk betydelse, eller vilken bok en passage kommer från?
target_construct: recurring symbolic semantic structure across documents
proxy_measure: sentence embeddings of each symbol's context, UMAP and HDBSCAN clusters
conclusion_en: Book centring reduced document identity as a confounder substantially but did not remove it, and reduced book dependence does not show that the remaining clusters are symbolic.
conclusion_sv: Bokcentrering minskade dokumentidentiteten som störfaktor tydligt men tog inte bort den, och mindre bokberoende visar inte att de återstående klustren är symboliska.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Largest book's share of a cluster (mean)
diagnostics.interpretation: Subtracting each book's mean vector lowers book dominance, but most clusters are still led by one book.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Clusters reviewed by a person
diagnostics.interpretation: Whether a cluster is about a symbolic meaning is a judgement a person has to make by reading it; until then no cluster is named.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Change in map trustworthiness (book-centred minus baseline)
diagnostics.interpretation: The 2-D map keeps about as much of the neighbourhood structure after centring; the improvement did not cost the map its fidelity.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Change in book entropy of clusters (book-centred minus baseline)
diagnostics.interpretation: Clusters mix books more evenly after centring. This shows the confounder was reduced, not that the remaining clusters are symbolic.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Occurrences in clusters drawn from several books
diagnostics.interpretation: About three times as many occurrences sit in cross-book clusters as in the baseline, still a minority.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Occurrences in clusters drawn from several books
diagnostics.interpretation: Few occurrences sit in clusters that span books, the pattern a symbolic structure across documents would need.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Largest book's share of a cluster (mean)
diagnostics.interpretation: The baseline map groups passages largely by book; most clusters are dominated by one text, its translator and style.

confounders.diagnostic: mean largest book share; cross-book occurrence share
confounders.mitigation: subtract each book's mean vector (book_centered); paratext cleaning
confounders.remaining_risk: most clusters are still led by one book

confounders.effect: clusters can form around the word rather than its context
confounders.mitigation: mask the matched word ([SYMBOL]) in a separate experiment

confounders.diagnostic: clusters flagged as paratext before and after cleaning

question_en: Do these texts represent the world's myth and folklore?
question_sv: Representerar texterna världens myter och folksagor?
target_construct: symbolic language of myth and folklore in general
proxy_measure: a hand-picked corpus of public-domain English texts and translations
conclusion_en: The atlas describes its own corpus. It cannot speak for folklore as a whole.
conclusion_sv: Atlasen beskriver sin egen korpus. Den kan inte tala för folksagor i allmänhet.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Books and traditions in the corpus
diagnostics.interpretation: A small, English-language, mostly European selection; findings describe these texts, not folklore as a whole.

question_en: Do these indicators measure how Sweden is doing?
proxy_measure: employment, sick leave, health and trust indicators from official sources
conclusion_en: A set of partial indicators, shown side by side, not a measure of wellbeing.
conclusion_sv: En uppsättning delindikatorer, visade sida vid sida, inte ett mått på välbefinnande.

diagnostics.diagnostic: Indicators as proxies
diagnostics.interpretation: Each indicator is a partial proxy; together they are not a single objective measure of wellbeing, and no index combines them.
